summary: Audited getDocumentationHandoff against the spec (§5.4). Confirmed drift: (1) two READY_FOR_DEVELOPER branches for wpsNotYetReviewed removed per spec v2.0.0 upstream-catch-all removal; (2) all-terminal early exit over all wpDetails added; (3) final fallthrough changed from READY_FOR_SYNTHESIS to WAIT; (4) hasPassedEffectiveUpstream local closure replaced with hasPassedDynamicUpstream from WP-001; (5) wpsWithDocFail filter now also gates on hasPassedDynamicUpstream. 5 tests updated to assert spec-correct behavior. Build: clean. Tests: 1871 pass.

comments.note: getDocumentationHandoff had two READY_FOR_DEVELOPER branches for `wpsNotYetReviewed` that spec v2.0.0 explicitly removed. The original code was added before the spec clarification and drifted. The all-terminal early exit was also missing — the function had scattered READY_FOR_SYNTHESIS returns that conflated 'all docWps passed' with 'all WPs are terminal', which are only equivalent after completePipeline has run.

summary: AC1 and AC3 pass. AC2 FAIL: wpsWithDocFail filter adds hasPassedDynamicUpstream gate not present in the spec, causing divergent behavior when upstream regresses after a documentation FAIL. Spec returns IN_PROGRESS (documentation self-reworks); implementation falls through to WAIT. Fix or spec-update required before proceeding.

comments.note: AC2 FAIL: wpsWithDocFail filter (workflow-handoff.ts ~line 1300) adds hasPassedDynamicUpstream(wp, 'documentation') as an extra gate not present in the spec. Spec (handoff.md §5.4 / Documentation Handoff) says: 'if any non-terminal, non-dependency-blocked WP with documentation in activeStages has FAIL documentation pipeline → return IN_PROGRESS'. No upstream-PASS gate is specified. The extra guard causes divergence when upstream regresses AFTER a documentation FAIL (code-review PASS → doc FAIL → code-review FAIL): spec returns IN_PROGRESS, implementation falls through to WAIT. Fix: remove the hasPassedDynamicUpstream guard from wpsWithDocFail OR update the spec first if the guard is intentional design.

No test covers the edge case: code-review PASS → documentation FAIL → code-review FAIL. The existing test at line 1581 only verifies the happy path (upstream still PASS when docs FAIL'd). Add a test for this scenario to lock in the correct behavior once the spec question is resolved.

AC1 met: all 5 spec branches correctly mapped and commented (all-terminal, readyForDocs, FAIL self-rework, upstream-in-progress WAIT, fallthrough WAIT). Old READY_FOR_DEVELOPER catch-all and wrong READY_FOR_SYNTHESIS fallthrough correctly removed.

summary: Rework: removed hasPassedDynamicUpstream(wp, 'documentation') gate from wpsWithDocFail filter in getDocumentationHandoff — spec §5.4 Condition 2 requires only non-terminal, non-dep-blocked, most-recent-doc-FAIL with no upstream-PASS prerequisite. Added inline comment explaining the spec rationale. Added regression test R4.4b: code-review:PASS → documentation:FAIL → code-review:FAIL → must return IN_PROGRESS (FAIL self-rework, no upstream gate). Build: clean. Tests: 1872 pass.

comments.note: No observations beyond the already-recorded debt note from implementation-1. Rework scope was narrow (single line removal + comment clarification).

comments.note: The inline comment at line 1297–1301 explicitly calls out why the upstream-PASS gate was absent from Condition 2 — this is clear and correctly references the Step 1 ordering as the reason upstream state is irrelevant by the time Condition 2 fires. Good self-documenting code.
No observations — rework was narrow (single line removal + comment). Code is clean and consistent with the spec.

summary: Reviewed 3 files (workflow-handoff.ts, workflow-handoff.test.ts, auto-handoff.test.ts). 0 Critical, 0 High, 0 Medium findings. All OWASP Top 10 categories reviewed. Security sign-off: PASS.

comments.note: No security findings — all OWASP Top 10 categories reviewed; no Critical or High issues identified. The change is a single-predicate removal (hasPassedDynamicUpstream gate) from the wpsWithDocFail filter, with an inline comment and a regression test. All inputs are TypeScript-typed WorkPackageDetail objects pre-validated by the schema layer; no user-controlled strings reach any interpreter; no new dependencies, cryptographic operations, or access-control paths introduced.

summary: Code review PASS with one reviewer-applied fix (Fix-Forward). The getDocumentationHandoff implementation correctly maps all four §5.4 branches. wpsWithDocFail filter is now spec-identical — no extraneous hasPassedDynamicUpstream gate. Regression test R4.4b correctly covers the cr:PASS → doc:FAIL → cr:FAIL → IN_PROGRESS edge case. Fix-Forward: corrected a logically-inverted inline comment that said 'If upstream has since regressed, Step 1 would have fired first' — Step 1 fires on upstream RE-PASS, not regression; updated comment to accurately describe both paths and cross-reference R4.4b.

comments.note: Fixed logically-inverted comment in getDocumentationHandoff Step 2 block (workflow-handoff.ts ~line 1204). Original: 'If upstream has since regressed, the re-engagement path in Step 1 would have fired first' — incorrect because Step 1 fires on upstream RE-PASS (via hasNewUpstreamPassSince), not on regression. Updated to: 'If upstream has since re-passed... Step 1 catches that case first... Condition 2 remains correct for all other upstream states, including when upstream has since regressed to FAIL (see R4.4b).' Non-behavioral change — no logic altered.

The four-branch structure of getDocumentationHandoff (all-terminal, ready-for-docs/re-engagement, FAIL self-rework, WAIT fallthrough) is clean and well-organized. Each branch is annotated with its spec §5.4 condition reference. The inline comment at Condition 2 explaining the absence of the upstream-PASS gate is a good self-documenting pattern — now corrected to be logically accurate.

Test R4.4b is well-constructed: the scenario is clearly described in the test name and body comments, the pipeline sequence (cr:PASS → doc:FAIL → cr:FAIL) accurately targets the intended edge case, and the assertion is minimal and precise. The regression test adds meaningful coverage for a non-obvious spec behavior.
